newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Stockpile sells 10,350 short tons aluminum.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Stockpile sells 10,350 short tons aluminum.

text.p: The U.S. Defense National Stockpile Center sold 10,350 short tons of aluminum at an average price of $1,604.74 a short ton, or 80.23 cents a lb, the agency said.
As expected, Allied Deals won the bulk of the offering, buying 7,750 tons at an average price of $1,604.24 a ton, or 80.21 cents a lb.
Trans-World Inc., which bought 550 tons at $1,608.44 a ton (80.42 cents a lb).
Alcan Aluminum Corp., which bought 500 tons at $1,610.02 a ton (80.50 cents a lb).
Reynolds Metals, which bought 500 tons at $1,607 a ton (80.35 cents a lb).
Global Metals & Minerals, which bought 500 tons at $1,599.15 a ton (79.96 cents a lb).
VAW of America, which bought 300 tons at $1,608 a ton (80.40 cents a lb).
Alcoa, which bought 250 tons at $1,604 a ton (80.20 cents a lb).
The London Metal Exchange closing cash price was 78.11 cents a lb Tuesday, the day the bids were opened.
The Stockpile yielded $16,609,027 in the sale.
